records.name: Science on Tap Philadelphia
records.summary: A monthly talk series for adults curious about science, history and the natural world, run by a group of Philadelphia museums. Talks take place on a Monday evening at a bar and restaurant in Old City, and the series aims for a lively feel rather than a classroom lecture.
records.what_you_do: Come listen to a speaker on one topic for about an hour, then mix with the crowd afterward.

schedule.text: Monthly talk on the second Monday of the month, starting at 6 pm.

locations.label: National Mechanics bar and restaurant, Old City

cost.text: The series site describes its events as free or low cost. Per-event prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Come to a monthly talk on the second Monday, or write to the series email with questions first.
first_step.basis: Talks are open to the public and need no membership. The site describes welcoming, accessible programming, but has no beginner program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect one expert talking about one topic, usually for about an hour, then time to mix with the crowd. The site says events usually draw about 100 people. Admission is free or low cost, and the site does not print a price for each talk.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the venue before you go, since special editions can move. The August 2026 talk was held at Benjamin Franklin Hall.
Arrive a little early, since events usually draw about 100 people.
The site does not describe step-free access, so email the series ahead of time with any access questions.

records.notes: All 2026 listings on the events page (February to September) are Mondays at 6 pm, and the newest is September 14, 2026. The venue can change for special editions. The street address is not printed on the site. The mission page says five institutions run the series, while the home page gives both five and six, so the record uses the general wording. The collaborate page says the Get on the List form may not be live yet, so email is the reliable route. Tier 1 phrase 'per the 2026 event listings' was removed from schedule text.

records.name: SEAMAAC
records.summary: A nonprofit that has helped immigrant and refugee families in Greater Philadelphia since 1984. Young people can join an afternoon arts program at Furness High School, and adults can volunteer by phone.
records.what_you_do: Young people can join the Urban Arts Entrepreneurship Program after school at Furness High School, with classes in breakdancing, deejaying, music production and visual arts, and summer sessions too. Adults can call the main line to talk about volunteering. The group's volunteer teams cover health and social services, education, community development and hunger relief.

schedule.text: The Urban Arts Entrepreneurship afterschool program at Furness High School runs Monday to Friday, 2:30 to 5 pm, with summer sessions as well.

locations.label: Furness High School (Urban Arts afterschool program)

cost.text: The site does not list program fees.

first_step.how: Call SEAMAAC at 215-467-0690 and ask how a young person joins the Urban Arts afterschool program at Furness High School.
first_step.basis: The program page names the program and a phone route, but does not say how a young person enrolls or who qualifies.
first_step.what_to_expect: Youth meet at Furness High School on weekday afternoons, from 2:30 to 5 pm, and take arts classes in breakdancing, deejaying, music production and visual arts. The site does not say how many young people attend or what to bring, so ask when you call.
first_visit_tips: Ask on the call what paperwork is needed before the first day, since the site does not list it.
Plan the trip for the 2:30 to 5 pm window, since that is when the program runs.
Ask about summer dates on the call, because the site does not print them.

records.notes: The program lists weekday afternoon hours at Furness High School but gives no ages, fees, enrollment steps or summer dates, so the first step is a phone call. Contact page emails and two home page links point to an internal host (seamaac-local), so no email is recorded and those links were not followed. The site says most staff speak more than one language and that its Red Cards resource sheets come in 43 languages, but it does not say which programs use which language, so no language codes are set. Truancy Case Management, the other youth program, works by referral through schools and truancy court and is not a join route, so it is left out. The education page names Career Connected Learning (C2L) as a partner (see leads_only). The one web search found no 2026 evidence on SEAMAAC's own pages, and older third-party listings disagree on the school (one says the program moved to South Philadelphia High School in 2018). The group's own page places it at Furness, so that is used. Nothing from the lead-only sites was recorded. Status stays probably_active because the site is current but shows no dates.

records.name: Seger Park Dog Owners Association
records.summary: Volunteers who look after the off-leash dog park in Seger Park. They run the dog run, organize neighborhood cleanups, and host community events with local businesses and musicians.
records.what_you_do: Dog owners use the park under posted rules and can join the association as members, which helps pay for upkeep. The association handles turf care, litter and trash removal, and restocks waste bags. Its site does not say how to sign up for a cleanup, so ask by email first.

schedule.text: The park runs around the clock, every day of the week.

cost.text: Membership is a suggested yearly donation: $50 for a household, or $25 for students and seniors. The site describes no fee for using the park itself.

requirements.gear: A dog that is licensed and vaccinated, a collar for use in the run, and a leash of 6 feet or less outside the run.

first_step.how: Read the park rules on segerdogpark.org, then use the membership page if you want to join for a suggested $50 a year, or $25 for students and seniors.
first_step.basis: The rules apply to everyone who enters, and the site names no membership requirement to use the park. Joining is through a donation page with no step-by-step sign-up, so the way in is simple but not spelled out.
first_step.what_to_expect: Bring your dog and follow the posted rules: stay inside the park, keep your dog in view and under voice control, and clean up after it. The site does not say how long visits last or who usually comes. Membership is a suggested yearly donation that helps pay for upkeep.
first_visit_tips: Your dog must be licensed and vaccinated, and the site points to ACCT Philly for licensing.
Kids aged 10 or younger are not allowed in the dog run, and those aged 11 to 15 need an adult with them.
Dogs must wear collars in the run, and leashes must be 6 feet or shorter outside it.
The park supplies biodegradable waste bags, and shovels and rakes are kept by the shed.

records.notes: Status is set to dormant under the status rule. The events page's newest dated item is December 2, 2023 (a holiday event), and the calendar page lists no dated events and shows a 2019 footer. The park itself is open and the rules page reads as current, so the verdict stays publish. Please review the status. The Woofstock summer concert series is listed on the events page as Tuesday evenings from May to September with no year, so it is not in schedule. Tier 1 said volunteers email the president; the group's pages do not say that, so the claim is not carried over. The membership page gives suggested dues and a donate route but no sign-up steps. The site does not mention gates, surfaces, benches or dog-size areas. Kids 10 and under may not enter the dog run, so kids_ok is left out and the rule is in first_visit_tips. ACCT Philly is named on the rules page for dog licensing. The contact name comes from IRS and NCCS tier 1 records, not from the site.

records.name: SEPTA Youth Advisory Council
records.summary: A nonprofit of young transit riders in Southeastern Pennsylvania. Members give feedback to SEPTA, educate riders, and push for student transit passes on campuses.
records.what_you_do: Apply online to join. Members give SEPTA input, table on college campuses, track transit laws, and run trainings such as a UPass training. The council also publishes a quarterly newsletter.

first_step.how: Create an account on septayac.org, then complete the application on the Apply page. You must be 18 to 25 and live or go to school in Philadelphia, Bucks, Chester, Delaware or Montgomery county.
first_step.basis: Members must apply online, review runs on a rolling basis with earlier applicants first, and the council only contacts applicants it wants to move forward with.
first_step.what_to_expect: Members give SEPTA input on transit, table on campuses, track transit law, and run trainings. The site does not say how often members meet, how much time it takes, or whether members are paid. It notes that members often juggle full-time jobs or school alongside the council.
first_visit_tips: Apply early, since review is rolling and earlier applicants get looked at first.
Check your age and where you live or study before you start, since both are rules for joining.
Send questions to contact@septayac.org before you apply.
The events page lists trainings such as the UPass training, a good sample of what members do.

records.notes: The Apply page and About page give the age range (18 to 25) and the residence rule (live or attend school in Philadelphia, Bucks, Chester, Delaware or Montgomery county), both now in the record. The events page lists a UPass training dated September 26 with no year, so it is not used as dated evidence, and last_sign_of_life is left out. The newsletter has no issue dates. No page states meeting schedule, time commitment or pay. The About page gives the founding as September 2009. The Apply page points to Idealist for open positions; Idealist is lead-only, so it was not read.

records.name: Shine Arts Alliance
records.summary: A Philadelphia arts group that works with young artists in performing, visual and media arts. It runs public fundraising events, and its youth arts initiative is listed as coming soon.
records.what_you_do: Young artists can take part in the group's arts education work. Its Shine Arts Academic Afterschool Initiative is listed as coming soon, with a registration form. The public can buy tickets to its fundraising events, such as its annual skate night.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the October 22, 2026 skate night fundraiser on the events page, or call 215-651-4763 to ask about the youth arts initiative.
first_step.basis: The youth initiative is listed as coming soon, and no class dates or costs are published, so the way in is not yet clear. Its registration form asks whether it is a first visit, which is a good sign, and the public fundraiser is open to ticket buyers.
first_step.what_to_expect: The fundraiser is a Thursday evening skate night from 6 to 9 pm at Rolling Thunder Skating Center on Roosevelt Boulevard. The ticket is $20 plus a $0.50 service fee and includes admission, skate rental and a meal. The site does not describe how youth classes run, how long they last, or who attends them.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-651-4763 before you visit the office, because the site gives no access or parking details.
The office is on the 3rd floor, so ask about building access when you call.
Skate rental is included with the fundraiser ticket, so you do not need your own skates.
Ask whether the youth initiative has opened for sign-ups, since the site lists it as coming soon.

records.notes: The events page lists a 4th annual performing arts skate fundraiser on October 22, 2026, 6 to 9 pm, at Rolling Thunder, with no youth class start dates. The education page says the afterschool initiative is coming soon and asks whether attendance will be physical or online. Tier 1 had the fundraiser price in cost and the fundraiser date in schedule; both are one time items, so they moved into first_step and what_to_expect, and cost and schedule are left out. Tier 1 commitment one_off and online_ok false are removed because class commitment is unpublished and the registration form offers online attendance. The contact page gives 100 South Juniper Street, 3rd Floor, and one page read gave a ZIP that could not be confirmed, so no ZIP is recorded for that office. The contact page email is connect@shineartsalliance.org. The contact name comes from IRS and NCCS tier 1 records.
